title: Share Trading Policy
date_approved: Approved by the Board effective 1 August 2024
date_next_review: Reviewed periodically by the Board; no date stated

tiers.name: directors, employees, contractors, consultants and other personnel
tiers.description: Everyone the policy applies to: a director or employee of Xero or its subsidiaries, or a contractor, consultant or other personnel who has agreed to comply with Xero's policies. All substantive prohibitions (derivatives and protection arrangements, short-term and speculative dealing, short selling) and the clearance requirements for margin lending, secured financing, grants of security and stock lending apply to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: A director or the CEO of Xero; a direct report of the CEO or someone who reports to a person who reports directly to the CEO; a person on the list of Designated Persons maintained by the Company Secretary team; or anyone notified that they are subject to trading restrictions. Must request clearance to deal at all times, not only in Closed Periods.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; a Designated Person distinguished only by the clearance approver (Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee and Company Secretary).

tiers.name: Director, CEO or CFO
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, the CEO and the CFO; Designated Persons distinguished by their clearance approver (Chair and Company Secretary) and, for directors, by a post-dealing notification duty to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: The Company Secretary; a Designated Person whose own clearance comes from the Chair and CEO.

tiers.name: All other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Designated Persons other than the Chair, directors, CEO, CFO and Company Secretary; clearance from the Company Secretary or delegate.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Close family members who are likely to act, or do act, on your instructions or advice about the purchase or sale of securities (spouse, partner, minor children or other dependants, and your partner's minor children or dependants); a company or trust controlled by you or your close family members or your family trust; and a family trust of which you are a trustee, beneficiary or director of the trustee company.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities; and an arrangement or transaction that is designed or intended to hedge (or otherwise limit) your economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities (e.g. unvested employee share plan shares); or otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.

windows.start_anchor: close of trade on the ASX on 31 March each year, or if that date is not a trading day, the last trading day before that day
windows.end_anchor: 10.00am Sydney time on the next trading day after Xero's full-year financial results are released to the ASX (usually early/mid May)

windows.start_anchor: close of trade on 30 September each year, or if that date is not a trading day, the last trading day before that day
windows.end_anchor: 10.00am Sydney time on the next trading day after Xero's half-year financial results are released to the ASX (usually early/mid November)

windows.start_anchor: any other period that the Board sets from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may set 'any other period' as a Xero Closed Period from time to time. The policy does not say whether such a period is announced or kept confidential, and clearance refusals must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Flat ban on derivative-market transactions in products based on Xero Securities, expressly extended to OTC products and to caps and collars, with no vesting or venue carve-out. Approval may be applied for only 'in exceptional circumstances'; the ordinary clearance route in section 6 is not available for a derivative.
rules.evidence: You must not engage in transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities. This includes OTC products, depository receipts, contracts for difference, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, exchange-traded options, caps and collars and any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban over unvested Xero Securities: the exceptional-circumstances approval route that exists for other derivative transactions is expressly closed for unvested securities.
rules.evidence: You may apply for approval to enter into one of these transactions in exceptional circumstances. Approval will not be given in relation to unvested Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Express ban on any arrangement or transaction designed or intended to hedge or otherwise limit economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities, with approval expressly unavailable.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that: is designed or intended to hedge (or otherwise limit) your economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities (e.g. unvested employee share plan shares)

rules.detail: 'Restricted' Xero Securities are treated alongside unvested securities in the hedging ban, so vested shares still subject to a plan restriction or holding lock cannot be hedged. The policy does not say whether the 'approval will not be given' carve-out extends to restricted (as opposed to unvested) securities.
rules.evidence: is designed or intended to hedge (or otherwise limit) your economic exposure to unvested or restricted Xero Securities (e.g. unvested employee share plan shares)

rules.detail: Hedging vested unrestricted shares is caught twice: by the catch-all in the derivatives sentence ('any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities', which is not limited to unvested holdings) and by the ban on arrangements that enable you to profit from a decrease in the market price. Exceptional-circumstances approval is theoretically available for vested holdings.
rules.evidence: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that: ... otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named as such, but forward contracts and swaps are expressly listed in the banned derivative products, so a prepaid forward or share swap is prohibited. A monetisation structured as a loan secured on Xero Securities is instead permitted with clearance under the secured financing paragraph.
rules.evidence: This includes OTC products, depository receipts, contracts for difference, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, exchange-traded options, caps and collars

rules.detail: Short selling is expressly included in the ban on short-term or speculative dealing, subject only to the exceptional-circumstances clearance route. Defined as borrowing and selling securities hoping to buy them back at a lower price.
rules.evidence: You must not deal in Xero Securities on a short term or speculative basis (including short selling), except in exceptional circumstances and with prior clearance to deal (see section 6).

rules.section: 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Stock lending is expressly permitted subject to prior clearance under the section 6 process, whether or not the person is a Designated Person. No conditions or price triggers are prescribed.
rules.evidence: Whether or not you are a Designated Person, you must seek clearance (in accordance with the process in section 6) before you: ... enter into a transaction that amounts to stock lending of your Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are named in the list of prohibited derivative-market products.
rules.evidence: This includes OTC products, depository receipts, contracts for difference, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, exchange-traded options, caps and collars

rules.section: 6; 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Margin loans are permitted with prior clearance for everyone, Designated Person or not. Transferring existing Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account is expressly caught as a separate clearance trigger.
rules.evidence: you must seek clearance (in accordance with the process in section 6) before you: enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangements (including transferring Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account)

rules.section: 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Granting a security or rights over Xero Securities is permitted subject to prior clearance; the wording 'or rights' is wider than a formal charge and would capture a bank's control or set-off rights over collared shares. It is also a dealing under section 3 as a creation of an interest in Xero Securities.
rules.evidence: grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities

rules.section: 6; 8 (Clearance required for any grant of security over Xero Securities, margin lending arrangements or stock lending)
rules.detail: Secured financing is not banned. Any margin loan 'or other secured financing arrangement' requires prior clearance through the section 6 process, and section 6 confirms that even non-Designated Persons must obtain clearance for it. The policy imposes no vesting restriction on collateral and no ongoing disclosure obligation.
rules.evidence: you will need to seek clearance to deal in Xero Securities if you want to deal during a Xero Closed Period (in exceptional circumstances), enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, or grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.

rules.detail: Buy-sell window test: buying and selling listed securities within a 6 month period is short term dealing and is prohibited except in exceptional circumstances with prior clearance. Selling within 6 months of acquisition through vesting or exercise under an employee equity plan is carved out.
rules.evidence: Short term dealing is the buying and selling of listed securities within a 6 month period. This can be a key indicator of insider trading, particularly if undertaken on a regular basis or in large amounts.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee and Company Secretary or their respective delegates
clearance.evidence: Chair | Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee and Company Secretary or their respective delegates

clearance.approver: Chair and Company Secretary or their respective delegates
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, ideally by close of business on the day of any dealing
clearance.evidence: If you are a director, you must promptly notify the Company Secretary (ideally by close of business on the day of any dealing) that you have entered into a dealing in Xero Securities.

clearance.approver: Chair and CEO or their respective delegates
clearance.evidence: Company Secretary | Chair and CEO or their respective delegates

Designated Persons need to request clearance to deal in Xero Securities at all times. ... After receiving dealing clearance, you must complete your dealing within 5 business days of the confirmation (or as specified in the confirmation), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.

clearance.tier: directors, employees, contractors, consultants and other personnel
clearance.approver: Company Secretary (or their delegate) at tradingclearance@xero.com
clearance.evidence: If you are not a Designated Person you do not require clearance to deal in Xero Securities (within the terms of this policy) outside Xero Closed Periods. However, you will need to seek clearance to deal in Xero Securities if you want to deal during a Xero Closed Period (in exceptional circumstances), enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, or grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.

short_term.basis: buying and selling within a 6 month period
carve_outs: Selling Xero Securities within 6 months after they have been acquired through the vesting or exercise of a Xero Security granted under an employee equity plan
exceptional circumstances with prior clearance to deal
short_term.evidence: Selling Xero Securities within 6 months after they have been acquired through the vesting or exercise of a Xero Security granted under an employee equity plan is not regarded as a short term dealing under this policy.

exceptions.approver: Company Secretary (or their delegate), or for Designated Persons the approvers in the section 6 table
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are rare, and may include severe financial hardship, a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking, and any other circumstance warranted in the individual situation.
a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking

trade under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where you did not have inside information when you entered into the plan, did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Closed Period, the plan does not permit you to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan, and the plan cannot be cancelled during a Closed Period other than in exceptional circumstances

deal in Xero Securities if there is no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Xero Securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which you are a beneficiary)
dispose of Xero Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

acquire Xero Securities under an employee equity plan (this exception applies to allocation or vesting but does not apply to selling Xero shares on market to cover tax or to cover the exercise price, exercising options or any subsequent dealings)
acquire Xero Securities under any dividend reinvestment plan operated by Xero

deal in a publicly offered diversified fund or scheme (but not a scheme of which Xero Securities are a significant portion) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party (e.g. an index fund)

external_documents: List of Designated Persons maintained by the Company Secretary team
exemption_authority: The Company Secretary (or delegate), and for Designated Persons the approvers in the section 6 table, may grant clearance to deal in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or court enforceable undertaking, 'any other circumstance warranted in the individual situation'), including during a Closed Period. The same exceptional-circumstances route is the only way to obtain approval for a derivative or protection arrangement, but approval will not be given in relation to unvested Xero Securities.
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand insider trading law (Xero is a New Zealand incorporated company listed on the ASX)
ASX Listing Rule 12.10 and director disclosure obligations under the ASX Listing Rules

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not engage in transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities. This includes OTC products ... caps and collars and any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is one of the few ASX policies that names 'collars' and 'OTC products' expressly, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are prohibited on their face rather than merely caught by a definition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional circumstances as the only derivatives gate
bespoke_clauses.clause: You may apply for approval to enter into one of these transactions in exceptional circumstances. Approval will not be given in relation to unvested Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar over vested shares is not absolutely barred, but it can only proceed through an exceptional-circumstances application (severe hardship, court order or similar), which a commercial monetisation is unlikely to satisfy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Whether or not you are a Designated Person, you must seek clearance ... before you: enter into a margin loan or other secured financing arrangements (including transferring Xero Securities into an existing margin loan account); grant a security or rights over your Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan and security legs of a funded collar are permitted with clearance, so the structure fails only on the derivative legs; a plain secured loan against Xero shares without a hedge is available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You must not enter into an arrangement or transaction that ... otherwise enables you to profit from a decrease in the market price of Xero Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This limb is not restricted to unvested holdings and independently catches the purchased put in a collar over fully vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Xero takes a 'substance over form' approach and has regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring around the derivatives ban (for example a non-recourse loan with an economically equivalent payoff, or a hedge booked at a Connected Person entity) will be assessed on its economic substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where clearance is required to deal under this policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not meet the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the permitted secured financing leg can be refused on reputational grounds alone, without reasons being given.

bespoke_clauses.clause: They may also decide to impose conditions on the dealing or withdraw the clearance at any time. If your clearance is not approved or is withdrawn, you must keep this fact confidential. Clearance is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of Inside Information prior to dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank cannot rely on a granted clearance surviving to signing or drawdown; it can be withdrawn at any time or lapse automatically, and the executive cannot explain why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Your Connected Persons should only deal in Xero Securities in circumstances where you yourself would be permitted to do so. Where clearance requirements would apply to your dealing, you must comply with those requirements on behalf of your Connected Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the derivatives ban or the clearance obligation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short term dealing is the buying and selling of listed securities within a 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with a tenor under six months, or one whose entry and physical settlement fall within six months, risks characterisation as short-term dealing on top of the derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no venue limitation and no vesting limitation on the derivatives ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: any other financial product that operates to limit the economic risk associated with Xero Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike venue-limited bans elsewhere, this catch-all covers OTC bank-written puts and calls over on-market as well as plan-sourced shares.

summary: A funded collar is effectively not possible under this policy. The financing legs are workable: a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement, a grant of security or rights over Xero Securities, and stock lending are all permitted with prior clearance under section 6, for Designated Persons and non-Designated Persons alike, with no restriction on using vested shares as collateral and no ongoing financier disclosure regime. The derivative legs, however, are expressly prohibited: section 8 bans transactions in the derivative markets involving products based on Xero Securities and specifically names OTC products, forward contracts, swaps and 'caps and collars', together with any other product that limits economic risk or enables the holder to profit from a price decrease, and that catch-all is not limited to unvested holdings. The only route is an application for approval in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or a comparable individual circumstance), which cannot be given at all over unvested Xero Securities and would rarely be granted for a commercial monetisation; any approval must also pass the Front Page Test, can be conditioned or withdrawn at any time, and must be exercised within 5 business days. Even if approved, the trade would have to fall outside the 31 March and 30 September Closed Periods and any Board-set period, avoid the six-month short-term dealing window, and be notified to the Company Secretary on the day if the holder is a director.
